title: Warm-start refits of motion kinds from the previous estimate
body:
When more poses of a moving part are observed, `MotionKindMixture.fit` refits every likely kind from scratch: each turning kind starts from a new free screw motion fit, and the sliding kind from the line through the first and the last observed origin. A robot that observes a door while opening it refits after every few new poses, and each refit repeats work whose result is already known.

## Warm start

Pass the previous mixture to the next fit, and start each kind's least-squares fit from that kind's previous estimate instead of from the free screw motion fit. From a good start, the fit needs only a few iterations. Every observation is still used and every number is still refitted, so the result is the same as a fit from scratch: no approximation, and nothing that a kind fitted earlier can lock in.

Open points:

- Kinds the previous mixture did not fit, because their probability was below `minimum_probability`, have no estimate and start from the free screw motion fit as today.
- The previous estimate holds a position for each earlier observation; the new observations need starting positions, for example by projecting their poses onto the previous screw axis.
- The classifier is rerun on all observations; it takes about 1.5 ms, so there is nothing to save there.

## Why not recursive updates yet

The fully recursive alternative carries each kind's fitted chart numbers and covariance forward as the prior of the next fit, updates the kind probabilities by how well each kind predicts the new poses, and drops the old poses. It costs the same for every update, but:

1. Early on, after a few degrees of a door, the posterior of the axis is far from Gaussian. A Gaussian carried forward from there is overconfident in the wrong place, and later poses cannot fully undo it. This is where a robot decides whether to act.
2. The Gaussian lives in a chart around the old estimate. When new poses move the estimate far, the prior is expressed around the wrong point, and the linearization errors add up.
3. The classifier gives probabilities given a summary of all poses, not likelihoods of new ones. Multiplying its answers for two batches of poses of the same part counts the shared axis twice.
4. Kinds below the cutoff have no posterior to carry forward, so they could never come back.
5. A fit of all poses can later recognise a jump of the tracker as an outlier; a recursive update has already absorbed it.

## Later: a hybrid for streaming trackers

When poses arrive fast, for example at 30 Hz, recursive updates between occasional fits of a sliding window of recent poses combine the constant cost of the first with the relinearization of the second, as incremental smoothers do. Each kind's Gaussian and the kind probabilities are then also what a belief state of the world would hold for the connection.
